Also, along the river the Tangut and the leaders of the Yiyueli clans before and behind the mountains all sent men bringing the patents, edicts, banners, and credentials Khitan had granted them to submit, all weeping and reporting their hardship, wishing to arm for revenge.
逸越利 is one tribal name, Yiyueli.
Iron Hu gate guards' heads fell off for no reason—Iron Hu was Chongrong's childhood name. He hated the omen but did not understand.
The heads of the iron Hu figures guarding Zhen's city gate fell off for no reason—Iron Hu was Chongrong's childhood name. He hated the omen but did not understand.
抱關鐵胡人 are iron statues of Hu gatekeepers.
At the city gate of Zhen the gate-keeping iron Hu men's heads fell off for no reason—"Iron Hu" was Chongrong's childhood name. Though he hated it, he did not understand.
At the city gate of Zhen the heads of the gate-keeping iron Hu figures fell off for no reason—"Iron Hu" was Chongrong's childhood name. Though he hated it, he did not understand.

Reaching Pozhou at Pojia Embankment, Gaozu sent Du Chongwei to meet him; the armies had joined battle when his general Zhao Yanzhi, who had a grudge against Chongrong, furled his banner mid-array and fled to the Jin army. His armor and saddle were all fitted with silver; Jin did not know he was coming over and vied to kill and divide him.

Reaching Pojia Embankment at Zongcheng, Gaozu sent Du Chongwei to meet him; the armies had joined battle when his general Zhao Yanzhi, who had a grudge against Chongrong, furled his banner mid-array and fled to the Jin army. His armor and saddle were all fitted with silver; Jin did not know he was coming over and vied to kill and divide him.
宗城破家堤: Pojia Embankment in Zongcheng; there is no Pozhou.
Chengde became Shunde; Zhen was renamed Heng, and Changshan Hengshan.
Chengde became Shunde; Zhen was renamed Heng, and Changshan became Hengshan.
Congjin first followed Zhuangzong in the army, became commander of the escort cavalry, and held the prefecture of Gui Prefecture.
Congjin first followed Zhuangzong in the army, became commander of the escort cavalry, and held the post of prefect of Gui Prefecture.
領貴州刺史: nominal prefect of Gui.
Congjin first followed Zhuangzong among the armies, became supreme commander of the escort cavalry, and held the prefecture of Gui Prefecture.
Congjin first followed Zhuangzong among the armies, became supreme commander of the escort cavalry, and held the post of prefect of Gui Prefecture.
領貴州刺史: nominal prefect of Gui.
After Fan Yanguang rebelled at Ye, Congjin already nursed rebellion, trusting the Yangzi barrier, gathering outlaws, and swelling his army.
After Fan Yanguang rebelled at Ye, Congjin already nursed rebellion, trusting the river as a barrier, gathering outlaws, and swelling his army.
江 here is the Han River at Xiangyang, not the Yangzi.
Gaozu tried to transfer him, saying: "The Prince of Dongping has come to court and returned home; Shangdang is open.
Gaozu tried to transfer him, saying: "Wang Jianli, Prince of Dongping, came to court wishing to return home and has already been moved to Shangdang.
東平王建立 is Wang Jianli; he asked to go home and was moved to Shangdang.
Gaozu was troubled and planned to move Congjin, sending someone to say: "The Prince of Dongping has come to court wishing to return home and has already been moved to Shangdang.
Gaozu was troubled and planned to move Congjin, sending someone to say: "Wang Jianli, Prince of Dongping, has come to court wishing to return home and has already been moved to Shangdang.
東平王建立 names Wang Jianli.
His son Hongchao served at court. Congjin asked to visit home and was refused.
His son Hongchao served at court. Congjin asked that his son be granted leave to come home, but he was not sent.
請賜告歸 asks leave for the son; it was the son who was not sent.
His son Hongchao was deputy commissioner of the palace parks and lived in the capital; Congjin asked leave to return home and was not sent.
His son Hongchao was deputy commissioner of the palace parks and lived in the capital; Congjin asked that his son be granted leave to return home, but the son was not sent.
請賜告歸 asks leave for the son.
Long afterward he became chief commander of You's horse and foot and garrisoned Wagong Pass.
Long afterward he became chief commander of You's horse and foot and garrisoned Waqiao Pass.
After long time he was made chief commander of You's horse and foot and garrisoned Wagong Pass.
After long time he was made chief commander of You's horse and foot and garrisoned Waqiao Pass.
Under Mingzong he governed Jiao, Ying, Ji, and Yi and was praised for his rule.
Under Mingzong he governed Gui, Ying, Ji, and Yi and was praised for his rule.
媯 is Gui Prefecture, not Jiao.
Under Mingzong he was prefect of Jiao, Ying, Ji, and Yi—renowned for his governance.
Under Mingzong he was prefect of Gui, Ying, Ji, and Yi—renowned for his governance.
媯 is Gui Prefecture, not Jiao.
When Gaozu rose at Taiyuan, the Last Emperor made Guangyuan Zhang Jingda's deputy. Khitan defeated them at Jin'an Stockade.
When Gaozu rose at Taiyuan, the Last Emperor made Guangyuan Zhang Jingda's deputy. Khitan defeated them, and they withdrew to hold Jin'an Stockade.
為契丹所敗，退守晉安寨: defeated, then withdrew to Jin'an.
Khitan besieged them until horses were eaten, then men, then they killed Jingda and surrendered.
Khitan besieged them until provisions ran out and they ate the horses; when the horses were gone they killed Jingda and surrendered.
殺馬而食，馬盡: they ate horses, not men.
Gaozu made him military governor of Xuanyi and chief of palace horse and foot.
Gaozu made him military governor of Xuanwu and chief of palace horse and foot.
宣武 is Xuanwu, not Xuanyi.
Jin Gaozu made Guangyuan military governor of Xuanyi and chief commander of the palace horse and foot.
Jin Gaozu made Guangyuan military governor of Xuanwu and chief commander of the palace horse and foot.
宣武 is Xuanwu, not Xuanyi.

When Guangyuan came to audience he feigned a gloomy air, always as if nursing some grievance; Gaozu suspected he felt slighted and sent to ask. He answered: "Your servant has no lack in wealth and honor—only that I did not die like Iron Zhang at the right place; this I am always ashamed of!

When Guangyuan came to audience he feigned a gloomy air, always as if nursing some grievance; Gaozu suspected he felt slighted and sent to ask. He answered: "Your servant has no lack in wealth and honor—only that I did not die like Zhang Shengtie at the right place; this I am always ashamed of!
張生鐵 is the personal name Zhang Shengtie.
Chengxun fled from Dan. The Deposed Emperor made him prefect of Zi and sent gifts—Guangyuan grew bolder and rebelled.
Chengzuo fled from Shan. The Deposed Emperor made him prefect of Zi and sent gifts—Guangyuan grew bolder and rebelled.
承祚 is Chengzuo; 單州 is Shan.

Chengxun fled back from Dan prefecture; the Deposed Emperor at once made Chengxun prefect of Zi and sent envoys with a jade belt and imperial horse to comfort him—Guangyuan grew all the more arrogant and then rebelled.

Chengzuo fled back from Shan prefecture; the Deposed Emperor at once made Chengzuo prefect of Zi and sent envoys with a jade belt and imperial horse to comfort him—Guangyuan grew all the more arrogant and then rebelled.
承祚 is Chengzuo; 單州 is Shan.

At that time the Deposed Emperor and Yelü Deguang faced each other between Cang and Wei; Yan observation and judging officer Dou Yi plotted in the army: "If we do not hold the Bo crossing with a strong force and great general, Ru can lead Khitan east across the river to join Guangyuan—then Henan is in peril!

At that time the Deposed Emperor and Yelü Deguang faced each other between Chan and Wei; Yun observation judge Dou Yi plotted in the army: "If we do not hold the Bo crossing with a strong force and great general, Ru can lead Khitan east across the river to join Guangyuan—then Henan is in peril!
澶 is Chan; 鄆州 is Yun.

Han Gaozu posthumously appointed Guangyuan Grand Secretary and enfeoffed him Prince of Qi, ordered Secretariat drafter Zhang Zheng to compose his stele inscription and give it to Chengxin to carve in stone at Qing prefecture.

尚書令 is Director of the Department of State Affairs/Secretariat, not Grand Secretary.
